title: Man. Post. Cap. VI: PLAC imputing/punishing the not-yet-existent paradox tip
pass_a_gloss: The punishing decree presupposes the existence and sin of the one punished. To impute sin to one not yet existing, or punish one not yet existing, Placeus calls a paradox. Tip before Cap. VII on the three similitudes.
pass_b_english: This latter presupposes the existence and the sin of him who is punished. For to impute sin to one not yet existing, to punish one not yet existing, seems to me a paradox.
source_text: Hoc supponit existentiam & peccatum illius qui punitur. Imputare enim peccatum nondum existenti, punire nondum existentem, mihi paradoxum videtur.

lemmas.gloss: to impute … to one not yet existing
to punish one not yet existing

choices.choice: Imputing/punishing the not-yet-existent is paradox; Cap. VI tip
